headline: Financial LLM trading-agent review reports disclosed gaps in shock resilience and security controls
summary: The arXiv v1 paper introduces FARSIGHT, a codebook-based method for reviewing published financial LLM trading-agent schemes across market-shock robustness and security controls. It is a scheme-level expert-review framework, not an automated benchmark suite or a live test of deployed agents. Applying it to 15 selected academic schemes, the authors report that 80% lacked evidence for at least one core robustness metric and 100% had at least one security weakness under their codebook. In a five-agent comparison, the LLM-based evaluator disagreed with human ratings on 24/45 metric cells (53.3%) and performed poorly on some newly defined threats. The ratings reflect what papers document, not confirmed absence from implementations; no proprietary production agents or live market behavior were evaluated.
